Shape the future of complex engineering programs in a high-visibility configuration management role.   
   An innovative and growing Australian engineering organisation is seeking an experienced Configuration Manager to lead, mature and continuously improve configuration management across complex systems, equipment and software programs. This is a hands-on, high-impact opportunity for someone who enjoys building structure, driving governance and partnering closely with engineering, project and delivery teams.   
   
  Your New Company  
   
 This is a rare opportunity to join a forward-thinking engineering business with a strong reputation for technical excellence, innovation and long-term project delivery. Based in a beautiful location, the organisation offers the best of both worlds: meaningful, visible project work within a supportive environment that values collaboration, capability uplift and career development. 
   
 You will be surrounded by excellent leadership and mentorship, with genuine access to senior decision-makers, clear progression pathways and the opportunity to make your mark on projects that matter. 
   
  Your New Role  
   
 As Configuration Manager, you will take ownership of the configuration management framework across complex engineering programs. This role blends strategic governance with practical delivery, giving you the autonomy to shape processes while remaining close to the technical detail. 
 
 Own, maintain and continuously improve configuration management policies, processes, procedures and tools. 
 Establish and govern configuration baselines across the full system lifecycle. 
 Lead configuration control activities, including Change Control Boards. 
 Manage engineering change processes, configuration status accounting and configuration audits. 
 Maintain accurate configuration records, drawings, specifications and associated technical data. 
 Provide practical CM guidance to engineering, project and delivery teams. 
 Support compliance with relevant defence, engineering and industry standards. 
 
  What You'll Need to Succeed  
 
 Significant configuration management experience within defence, aerospace or complex engineering environments. 
 Experience developing and implementing CM frameworks, policies and procedures. 
 Strong understanding of configuration data, baselines and engineering change processes. 
 Knowledge of relevant CM standards such as EIA-649, MIL-HDBK-61, ISO, ITIL or equivalent. 
 Hands-on experience using CM or PLM tools; Windchill experience will be highly regarded. 
 Ability to operate strategically while also supporting hands-on delivery. 
 Strong stakeholder engagement skills across technical and project teams. 
 A degree in Engineering, Systems Engineering, IT or a related discipline. 
 
  What's in it for you  
 
 Excellent leadership, mentorship and support from experienced senior leaders. 
 Clear progression opportunities within a growing and highly visible organisation. 
 Exposure to complex, meaningful engineering projects with genuine technical depth. 
 The chance to shape and improve configuration management capability from the ground up. 
 A collaborative, innovative and dynamic working environment. 
 Beautiful location with access to an enviable lifestyle and engaging project work. 
 Strong company visibility, where your contribution will be recognised and valued. 
 
  What to do now:  
   
 If you are a hands-on Configuration Manager looking for a role with autonomy, visibility, mentorship and long-term career growth, this is an opportunity worth exploring.

## Chief Information Officer
## Position Overview
We are looking for a visionary and commercially astute Chief Information Officer (CIO) to lead our organisation's information and communications technology strategy, operations, and governance. This is a senior executive role suited to an experienced technology leader who thrives at the intersection of business strategy and digital innovation. The successful candidate will be responsible for aligning ICT capabilities with organisational priorities, driving transformation, and ensuring the long-term integrity and security of our technology infrastructure.
## Key Responsibilities
- Analyse organisational information needs and define technology solutions that effectively support business objectives and operational performance
- Formulate, implement, and continuously refine ICT strategies, policies, and plans that align with the organisation's broader mission and priorities
- Lead the selection, procurement, and installation of ICT systems and infrastructure, ensuring solutions are scalable, reliable, and fit for purpose
- Direct ICT operations across the organisation, setting clear priorities between system development, ongoing maintenance, and day-to-day operations
- Oversee the organisation's cybersecurity posture, ensuring robust protections are in place to safeguard data, systems, and digital assets
- Drive digital transformation initiatives that improve organisational efficiency, enhance service delivery, and support innovation
- Develop and manage the ICT budget, ensuring effective allocation of resources and demonstrable return on technology investment
- Build, mentor, and lead high-performing ICT teams, fostering a culture of collaboration, continuous learning, and professional development
- Engage and manage relationships with external technology vendors, partners, and service providers to ensure contractual obligations and service standards are met
- Champion the rollout of user training programmes to ensure staff are equipped to effectively adopt and utilise ICT systems and tools
- Provide executive-level reporting and strategic advice to the Board and senior leadership team on technology risks, opportunities, and performance
- Ensure ICT systems and practices remain compliant with relevant legislation, industry standards, and data governance frameworks
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree or higher in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related discipline
- Demonstrated experience in a senior ICT leadership role, with a strong track record of delivering enterprise-wide technology strategy
- Proven ability to align ICT capability with organisational strategy and drive measurable business outcomes
- Strong understanding of cybersecurity principles, risk management, and data governance best practices
- Experience managing large-scale ICT budgets, procurement processes, and vendor relationships
- Excellent leadership and people management skills, with the ability to inspire, develop, and retain high-performing teams
- Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with a strategic mindset and the ability to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
- Sound knowledge of ICT infrastructure, cloud environments, enterprise systems, and emerging technologies
- High-level communication, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills across all levels of an organisation
## Preferred Qualifications
- Postgraduate qualification in Business Administration (MBA), Information Technology, or a related field
- Industry certifications such as ITIL, TOGAF, CISSP, or equivalent
- Experience leading digital transformation programmes within complex or large-scale organisations
- Familiarity with Australian data privacy legislation, including the Privacy Act 1988 and the Australian Privacy Principles
- Prior experience presenting to executive leadership teams or Boards of Directors
## Why Join Us?
- Play a pivotal role in shaping the digital future of a dynamic and growing organisation, with genuine influence at the executive level
- Access to ongoing professional development opportunities, including leadership programmes, industry conferences, and certifications
- Flexible working arrangements that support a healthy work-life balance
- Collaborative and inclusive workplace culture that values innovation, integrity, and continuous improvement
- Competitive remuneration package with performance-based incentives and additional employee benefits
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation

Job Title: Metallurgical Technician (Metallurgical or Materials Technician - ANZSCO 312912) 
Company: Scidell Pty Ltd, allied company of Multicom Resources Pty Ltd 
Location: St Elmo Site, Julia Creek QLD, Australia 
Employment Type: Permanent, Full-time 
Recruitment managed by: Yakr Pty Ltd

About the company:
Our client Scidell Pty Ltd is a scientific delivery alliancing company created to provide professional and cost-effective solutions to Multicom Resources Pty Ltd (Multicom). Scidell’s multi-disciplined scientific and technical project professionals operate from Brisbane and on-site to deliver major projects from initial study through to execution, commissioning, and ongoing expert operational support. 

Multicom is on a mission to bring high-purity critical minerals to the world and become a reliable supplier for global technology manufacturers. Currently, Multicom is progressing the permitting, approval, and development of its 100% owned Saint Elmo Project, situated 25 km east of Julia Creek in Queensland's Northwest Minerals Province , focused on advancing the production of critical assets like vanadium and high-purity alumina (HPA). 

About the role:
As a Metallurgical Technician at Scidell, you will be a key member of the production and operations team responsible for monitoring and improving metallurgical performance targets for the Saint Elmo refinery and mine facility. Working under the direct supervision of the Process Supervisor, you will test materials, operate equipment, and optimize processes to ensure safe, efficient plant operations. This role provides an outstanding opportunity to apply technical data analysis and hands-on testing skills within a highly sophisticated minerals processing environment. 

Key Responsibilities:
•	Process Optimization & Monitoring: Monitor various stages of the production process to ensure smooth operations. Check and adjust parameters such as temperature, pressure, flow rates, and chemical concentrations to maximize plant throughput, Vanadium/HPA recovery, and quality costs. 
•	Metallurgical Testing & Surveys: Undertake surveys, coordinate sampling activities, and execute test work to evaluate and identify process improvement opportunities. 
•	Equipment Operations: Start up, shut down, adjust, and operate plant machinery and equipment safely in strict accordance with standard operating procedures (SOPs). 
•	Equipment & Lab Performance: Monitor key equipment across both the process plant and the onsite laboratory to ensure components are optimized and alternative operational methods are assessed. 
•	Quality Control & Data Review: Conduct regular routine inspections and quality control checks on products and materials. Review operating and technical data to identify instances of noncompliance or opportunities for process optimization. 
•	Metallurgical Reporting: Maintain accurate records of equipment operations, process parameters, production, and testing activities. Generate precise metallurgical reconciliations and complete timely daily, weekly, and monthly reports. 
•	Troubleshooting & Technical Support: Identify and troubleshoot basic equipment issues, malfunctions, or process deviations. Provide expert technical support to operations, laboratory teams, and the senior process engineering team, collaborating closely on complex issues. 
•	Safety Compliance: Adhere strictly to the Site Safety and Health Management System and all established SOPs, ensuring all safety hazards or incidents are reported promptly. 

Key Requirements:
•	Education: Bachelor's degree in Extractive Metallurgy, Chemistry, or Chemical Engineering. 
•	Experience: Minimum of 5 years of experience in a similar metallurgical or materials testing role, with solid practical experience testing materials within a mineral/metal process and refinery environment. 
•	Licences: Possession of (or the immediate ability to acquire) a Radiation Safety Licence and a Queensland Driver’s Licence (manual preferred). 
•	Technical Skills: Sound understanding of process control systems , mechanical aptitude or a strong interest in hands-on technical roles , and a proven ability to source, gather, interpret, and communicate quantitative and qualitative data. 
•	Personal Attributes: Highly detail-oriented, safety-conscious, willing to learn, and possessing a reliable and consistent work ethic. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to follow technical instructions accurately. 
•	Pre-Employment Screening: Must be able to pass a comprehensive Pre-Employment Medical examination, including a drug and alcohol screen. 

Why join Scidell?
Scidell offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge mineral processing projects while working in a supportive, cooperative, and collaborative environment. Be part of a dedicated team that values safety, high attention to detail, and innovation in delivering critical minerals to global markets. 

How to Apply: 
If you're ready to be part of a dynamic team at Scidell Pty Ltd, dedicated to innovation and excellence, we’d love to hear from you! Please submit your resume/CV, ensuring you highlight your relevant material testing, metallurgical data analysis, and engineering experiences. 

Scidell Pty Ltd is an equal-opportunity employer, committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds. While we appreciate every application, please note that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.
